is_anopheles.evidence: Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles coluzzii were the major anophelines represented in all collections across the ecological zones (Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The L1014F kdr insecticide resistance mutation (kdr-w) is found at high frequency across all study sites... The L1014S mutation was also examined in a subset of samples (Abstract, Page 6).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Figure 4 (Page 7) provides genotype frequencies (kdr/kdr, kdr/S, S/S) for A. gambiae and A. coluzzii at four sites (Arid Savanna, Humid Savanna, Semi-Forest, Deep Forest) with sample sizes (n) for each group.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from four different study sites at the border with Mali and in Guinea Conakry (Fig. 1). Takan (N 11.47, W 8.33) and Toumani Oulena (N 10.83, W 7.81) are both small villages in the Yanfolila district of southern Mali... Koraboh... Kissidougou district... Guinea Conakry... Koundara... Macenta district... Guinea Conakry (Page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study describing original mosquito collections and molecular characterization.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is reported for specific villages: Takan, Toumani Oulena, Koraboh, and Koundara, with coordinates provided on Page 2.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: All reported collections occurred in October and November in 2012 (Page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study explicitly compares its 2012 data to a previous 2006 survey (Vezenegho et al. 2009), indicating these are new, independent collections.

supplement.evidence: Figure 4 provides extractable genotype frequencies and sample sizes. While Additional file 1 is mentioned as containing 'molecular attribute data', the primary data required is available in the main text and figures.

assessment.summary: The study characterizes Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles coluzzii populations across four ecological zones in Mali and Guinea Conakry. Mosquitoes were collected in October and November 2012 using human-landing captures, pyrethroid spray catches, and larval sampling. The study reports the frequency of the Vgsc L1014F (kdr-w) mutation, which was found at high frequency and near fixation in forest sites. Vgsc L1014S (kdr-e) was also screened but not detected in the samples tested. Genotype frequencies for L1014F are provided for each species and site in Figure 4.
